answer: Treat each agent identity like an ember kept in a vault under a glacier: the vault only opens after an independent verifier confirms the operator is a distinct real person, using a non-transferable institutional credential bound to one public key and recorded in a public revocation registry. A second identity from the same person is visible and rejected. So forging one fake identity costs an attacker a whole new verified real-world credential, plus fraud exposure if it is faked.
